title: Frontend: Copy to Clipboard
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Copy to Clipboard. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({adapter="success"}). Render controlled Text input and Copy button. The provided adapter mode simulates an async clipboard service: success resolves, reject rejects, missing is unavailable. On click await that adapter, show Copied or Copy unavailable in [data-testid="status"], and on success echo the submitted text in [data-testid="copied"]. This isolated exercise must not access the real system clipboard.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Invoke clipboard writing from a user gesture and await its promise.
alternativeApproaches: Add a copyable code block whose feedback resets when its source changes.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Successful copy; rejected permission; unavailable API.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
